en: The Philippine eagle has a wingspan of up to 2 meters, making it one of the largest forest eagles in the world.
The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed on June 12, 1898, exactly 377 years after Ferdinand Magellan arrived in 1521.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of a Senate with 24 members and a House with over 300 representatives.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but Filipino and English are the only two official languages used nationally.
The MassKara Festival in Bacolod features over 40 competing dance groups wearing vibrant smiling masks to celebrate local resilience.
Jose Rizal wrote his famous novels in Spanish and was executed at age 35 on December 30, 1896.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago, creating over 10,000 kilometers of stone-walled steps.
The Philippines is divided into 17 administrative regions, including the National Capital Region, which contains exactly 16 cities and one municipality.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and founded the country's first pediatric hospital in 1957.
The Sampaguita was chosen as the national flower in 1934 because it blooms all year round, symbolizing simplicity and strength.
Under the 1987 Constitution, citizens can vote for the President and 24 Senators once they reach the minimum voting age of 18.
National Artist Napoleon Abueva created over 500 artworks during his 60-year career, earning him the title of Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture.
